clips.title: The story
paras: Croaky's Head is the severed bounty from a menacing murloc leader who terrorized the roads of eastern Elwynn Forest. Bringing proof of the creature's death to the Stormwind guard at Ridgepoint Tower offers grim relief to a garrison grieving their fallen comrades. It marks an essential victory for local defenders struggling to secure Elwynn's contested waterways.

Murlocs along the rivers and streams of Elwynn Forest have grown increasingly bolder, ambushing unwary travelers and threatening vital trade routes. Among these aquatic raiders, Croaky stood out as a particularly aggressive chieftain, rallying other murlocs and leading attacks dangerously close to local roads. For merchants, farmers, and travelers moving between Elwynn and Redridge, the creature's presence turned peaceful roadways into deadly hazard zones. Striking down this aggressive raider halts a relentless series of ambushes, removing a brazen menace that openly challenged Stormwind's hold over the eastern woodland outskirts.

Ridgepoint Tower stands as Stormwind's easternmost sentinel post in Elwynn Forest, guarding the strategic crossing into Redridge Mountains. The guards stationed here, led by Officer Merell Ross, have found themselves stretched thin against the surrounding dangers. The escalating murloc aggression recently claimed the lives of two watchmen on patrol, shaking the outpost and highlighting just how vulnerable the border has become. Presenting Croaky's severed head to Officer Ross delivers tangible proof of retribution, lifting the beleaguered garrison's morale and giving the defenders an opening to finally drive the aquatic raiders back from Elwynn's borders.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: This murloc has no doubt been terrorizing the local roads for some time. You suspect the nearby watch guards will want to know of its demise.

clips.title: Completion
paras: We lost two members of the watch last week to the murlocs, adventurer. Hopefully with their leader slain, we can start pushing them out of Elwynn.
